card.name: Birth-defect wording in pregnancy warnings
card.fires_on: The word just before a birth-defect or fetal-harm term in pregnancy warnings, mostly the end of 'congenital' (before malformations or anomalies) and 'human' in 'known human teratogen'.

modes.label: congenital malformations
modes.description: The end of 'congen-ital' right before 'malformations' or 'anomalies' in fetal risk statements.
modes.example: Warfarin sodium exposure during pregnancy causes a recognized pattern of major congen<<ital>> malformations (warfarin embry

modes.label: known human teratogen
modes.description: 'human' in the phrase 'known human teratogen' for thalidomide-like drugs.
modes.example: Thalidomide is a known<< human>> teratogen that causes severe life-threatening

modes.label: can cause fetal harm
modes.description: A verb or drug-name end right before 'fetal harm' or similar risk wording.
modes.example: SPRAVATO may<< cause>> fetal harm when administered to pregnant women.
